# 👆 Click a mountain

This board is **one photograph with clickable zones on it** — and the zones are not ours: they are the *file's own*
[Commons image notes](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Scuol-Motta_Naluns,_11-10-2024._(actm.)_21.jpg), written
by the photographer, read out of the file's wikitext and converted to percentages of the picture. Six peaks, exactly
where that file says they are.

Hover a box (a tap reveals it on a phone) and its name appears. A click **publishes the name** on the picture card's
`selection` channel, which is the same event a gallery tile raises — so the 📄 Article Excerpt beside it, listening to
that channel, loads the mountain you clicked. No page reload; the URL never changes.

- `Piz Mezdi` is the odd one out: its line ends `open`, so it opens the article in a new tab instead of feeding the card.
- Zones live in the card's ⚙ panel as **text**, one per line — `x,y,w,h | label | kind | value | action`, with the box in
  percentages of the picture. Fix one by hand, or write a board that has them from the start.

The extract card starts at "waiting for a reference": that is the app's own state for a consumer whose producer has not
emitted yet, and the first click fills it.
